T05_Transformers.q: What losses occur in a transformer?
T05_Transformers.a: Core (iron) losses — hysteresis and eddy current; Copper losses — I²R in windings
opts: Core (iron) losses — hysteresis and eddy current; Copper losses — I²R in windings
T05_Transformers.exp: Core losses: constant (load-independent), reduced by laminated silicon steel core. Copper losses: I²R, proportional to load² — increase with load.

T05_Transformers.a: Transformer with single winding serving as both primary and secondary
opts: Transformer with single winding serving as both primary and secondary
T05_Transformers.exp: Auto-transformer: part of winding is common to input and output. More efficient for small voltage ratio changes. Used in motor starters (Korndörfer) and small voltage adjustments.

T05_Transformers.a: Change in secondary voltage from no-load to full load as percentage of rated voltage
opts: Change in secondary voltage from no-load to full load as percentage of rated voltage
T05_Transformers.exp: Good regulation = low percentage (small voltage change with load). Achieved by low leakage reactance and low winding resistance.

T05_Transformers.a: Output power / Input power × 100%; maximum at load where copper loss = iron loss
opts: Output power / Input power × 100%; maximum at load where copper loss = iron loss
T05_Transformers.exp: Maximum efficiency: iron losses (fixed) = copper losses (variable with load). Typically 95–99% for power transformers at optimal loading.

T05_Transformers.q: What is the purpose of transformer oil?
T05_Transformers.a: Provides insulation and cooling; dissipates heat from core and windings
opts: Provides insulation and cooling; dissipates heat from core and windings
T05_Transformers.exp: Transformer oil: mineral oil or synthetic, high dielectric strength (>30kV/mm), good thermal conductivity. Regular testing: dielectric strength, moisture content, dissolved gas analysis.

T05_Transformers.a: Gas and oil actuated protection relay for oil-filled transformers — alarms on slow gas accumulation, trips on sudden fault
opts: Gas and oil actuated protection relay for oil-filled transformers — alarms on slow gas accumulation, trips on sudden fault
T05_Transformers.exp: Buchholz relay: float switches in pipe between main tank and conservator. Gas accumulates on minor internal fault → alarm. Oil surge on major fault → trip. Very sensitive protection.

T05_Transformers.q: What does 'vector group' Dyn11 mean for a transformer?
T05_Transformers.a: Delta primary, star secondary with neutral, 30° phase shift (11 o'clock position)
opts: Delta primary, star secondary with neutral, 30° phase shift (11 o'clock position)
T05_Transformers.exp: Vector groups define winding connections and phase displacement. Dyn11: common for 11kV/440V distribution transformers. D=Delta primary, y=star secondary, n=neutral brought out, 11=330° (or -30°) phase shift.

T05_Transformers.q: What insulation class is typically used for dry-type transformers?
T05_Transformers.exp: Dry-type transformers: encapsulated resin or air-cooled. No oil fire risk — suitable for unmanned spaces, accommodation areas. Higher insulation class needed as no oil cooling.

T05_Transformers.q: What is dissolved gas analysis (DGA) for transformer oil?
T05_Transformers.a: Analysis of gases dissolved in oil to detect internal faults (overheating, arcing, insulation breakdown)
opts: Analysis of gases dissolved in oil to detect internal faults (overheating, arcing, insulation breakdown)
T05_Transformers.exp: DGA: key indicator of fault type. Acetylene = arcing. Ethylene = high temperature. Methane/ethane = moderate overheating. Hydrogen = corona. Used for early fault detection before failure.

T05_Transformers.a: ONAN (Oil Natural Air Natural), ONAF (Oil Natural Air Forced), OFAF (Oil Forced Air Forced)
opts: ONAN (Oil Natural Air Natural), ONAF (Oil Natural Air Forced), OFAF (Oil Forced Air Forced)
T05_Transformers.exp: ONAN: natural convection of oil and air. ONAF: forced air cooling fans. OFAF: oil pumped through radiators with forced air. Rating increases with each step.

T05_Transformers.q: What is the purpose of a 'conservator' tank on a transformer?
T05_Transformers.a: Expansion tank that accommodates oil volume changes with temperature, keeping main tank full
opts: Expansion tank that accommodates oil volume changes with temperature, keeping main tank full
T05_Transformers.exp: Conservator: small tank above main tank connected by pipe (Buchholz relay in pipe). As oil expands/contracts with temperature, level changes in conservator, main tank stays full.

T05_Transformers.q: What is the purpose of a 'tap changer' on a transformer?
T05_Transformers.a: Adjusts transformer ratio by changing number of turns, allowing voltage fine-tuning
opts: Adjusts transformer ratio by changing number of turns, allowing voltage fine-tuning
T05_Transformers.exp: Off-circuit tap changer (OCTC): must be de-energised to change. On-load tap changer (OLTC): changes taps under load using diverter switch. Allows ±5–10% voltage adjustment.

T05_Transformers.a: Polarity test — ensures transformers can be paralleled safely (same terminal markings)
opts: Polarity test — ensures transformers can be paralleled safely (same terminal markings)
T05_Transformers.exp: Polarity test: ensures additive or subtractive polarity. Critical when paralleling transformers — wrong polarity = circulating current = short circuit. Marked by dot convention or H1/X1 terminals.

T05_Transformers.q: What is the purpose of the silica gel breather?
T05_Transformers.a: Absorbs moisture from air entering conservator as oil cools and contracts, preventing wet oil
opts: Absorbs moisture from air entering conservator as oil cools and contracts, preventing wet oil
T05_Transformers.exp: Silica gel: blue when dry, pink when saturated. Check colour regularly; replace or regenerate (dry in oven) when pink. Wet oil leads to reduced dielectric strength and insulation failure.

T06_Sensors.q: What is an RTD (Resistance Temperature Detector)?
T06_Sensors.a: Temperature sensor whose resistance changes with temperature — typically platinum
opts: Temperature sensor whose resistance changes with temperature — typically platinum
T06_Sensors.exp: RTD: uses positive temperature coefficient of resistance. PT100: platinum, 100Ω at 0°C. Very accurate, stable, used for motor/generator winding temps, machinery monitoring.

T06_Sensors.a: Platinum RTD with 100 Ohms resistance at 0°C
opts: Platinum RTD with 100 Ohms resistance at 0°C
T06_Sensors.exp: PT100: standard resistance-temperature characteristic. At 100°C: ~138.5Ω. Linear over wide range. 2-wire, 3-wire, or 4-wire connections (3/4 wire eliminates lead resistance error).

T06_Sensors.q: What is the Seebeck effect (thermocouple principle)?
T06_Sensors.a: When two dissimilar metals are joined, a voltage (EMF) proportional to temperature difference is produced
opts: When two dissimilar metals are joined, a voltage (EMF) proportional to temperature difference is produced
T06_Sensors.exp: Seebeck effect: basis of thermocouple operation. Measure EMF at cold junction (reference) to determine temperature difference. Cold junction compensation needed for accurate measurement.

T06_Sensors.q: What is the difference between a thermocouple and an RTD?
T06_Sensors.a: Thermocouple: generates EMF (self-powered, fast, wide range); RTD: measures resistance change (accurate, stable, needs power supply)
opts: Thermocouple: generates EMF (self-powered, fast, wide range); RTD: measures resistance change (accurate, stable, needs power supply)
RTD uses voltage, thermocouple uses resistance
T06_Sensors.exp: Use thermocouple for: high temperatures (>600°C), fast response, remote exhaust sensing. Use RTD for: accurate moderate temperatures, motor windings, bearing temperatures.

T06_Sensors.q: What type of sensor is used for exhaust gas temperature on a diesel engine?
T06_Sensors.exp: Exhaust gas: 300–700°C range, fast response needed. Type K thermocouple: range -200 to +1260°C, most common. Type J: iron-constantan. Type T: copper-constantan (lower temperatures).

T06_Sensors.a: Converts pressure to electrical signal (typically 4–20mA or 0–10V) via strain gauge or piezoelectric element
opts: Converts pressure to electrical signal (typically 4–20mA or 0–10V) via strain gauge or piezoelectric element
T06_Sensors.exp: 4–20mA: standard industrial signal. 4mA = zero (live zero — wire break = 4mA, easy to detect). 20mA = full scale. Long distance transmission, noise-immune.

T06_Sensors.q: What is a flow meter and how does the electromagnetic type work?
T06_Sensors.a: Measures fluid flow rate; electromagnetic type: induced EMF in conductive fluid proportional to velocity (Faraday's law)
opts: Measures fluid flow rate; electromagnetic type: induced EMF in conductive fluid proportional to velocity (Faraday's law)
T06_Sensors.exp: Electromagnetic flow meter: magnetic field across pipe, conductive fluid flow induces EMF across electrodes. No moving parts, no pressure drop. For water, oil, seawater — not gases.

T06_Sensors.q: What is calibration of a sensor?
T06_Sensors.a: Verifying sensor output against known standard reference and adjusting if necessary to ensure accuracy
opts: Verifying sensor output against known standard reference and adjusting if necessary to ensure accuracy
T06_Sensors.exp: Calibration: use certified reference (pressure calibrator, temperature bath). Record as-found and as-left values. Certificate required for class surveyor. Interval: per PMS or after repair.

T06_Sensors.q: What is 'zero and span' adjustment on a transmitter?
T06_Sensors.a: Zero: sets output for minimum input (4mA); Span: sets output for maximum input (20mA)
opts: Zero: sets output for minimum input (4mA); Span: sets output for maximum input (20mA)
T06_Sensors.exp: Zero (4mA) and span (20mA) adjustment: fine-tune transmitter output to match actual range. Example: 0–10 bar pressure transmitter — zero sets 4mA at 0 bar, span sets 20mA at 10 bar.

T06_Sensors.q: What is a level sensor and types used on ships?
T06_Sensors.a: Detects liquid level; types: float switch, ultrasonic, radar, capacitance, differential pressure
opts: Detects liquid level; types: float switch, ultrasonic, radar, capacitance, differential pressure
T06_Sensors.exp: Float switch: simple on/off. Ultrasonic: non-contact, measures distance to surface. Radar: more accurate than ultrasonic for fuel/cargo. DP: measures pressure difference = head = level.

T06_Sensors.a: Detects presence of object without contact — inductive (metal detection) or capacitive types
opts: Detects presence of object without contact — inductive (metal detection) or capacitive types
T06_Sensors.exp: Inductive proximity: detects ferrous metal. Capacitive: detects any material. Used for: valve position feedback, shaft rotation counting, conveyor monitoring, safety interlocks.

T06_Sensors.q: What is a tachometer/speed sensor on diesel generators?
T06_Sensors.a: Measures shaft rotation speed — magnetic pickup (gear tooth sensor) or optical encoder
opts: Measures shaft rotation speed — magnetic pickup (gear tooth sensor) or optical encoder
T06_Sensors.exp: Magnetic pickup: generates pulses as gear teeth pass. Frequency = speed. Used for overspeed detection, governor feedback, synchronisation. Zero-speed detection for interlocks.

T06_Sensors.q: What is the purpose of a 4-20mA signal?
T06_Sensors.a: Standard analog signal for industrial instrumentation — live zero, immune to voltage drop, long distance capable
opts: Standard analog signal for industrial instrumentation — live zero, immune to voltage drop, long distance capable
T06_Sensors.exp: 4mA = 0%, 20mA = 100%. Live zero: 4mA in healthy circuit, so 0mA = broken wire. Loop powered: 24VDC supply, transmitter draws 4–20mA. No ground loops (current loop).

T06_Sensors.q: How do you verify a pressure transducer is working correctly?
T06_Sensors.a: Apply known pressures (dead weight tester or calibrated reference), check output 4–20mA matches expected values
opts: Apply known pressures (dead weight tester or calibrated reference), check output 4–20mA matches expected values
T06_Sensors.exp: Calibration procedure: isolate from process (isolation valve), apply reference pressure via deadweight tester or pressure calibrator, record mA output at multiple points (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% span).

T06_Sensors.q: What is a thermistor and how does it differ from PT100?
T06_Sensors.a: Thermistor: semiconductor, large resistance change with temperature (NTC: negative, or PTC: positive), less accurate than PT100 but very sensitive
opts: Thermistor: semiconductor, large resistance change with temperature (NTC: negative, or PTC: positive), less accurate than PT100 but very sensitive
T06_Sensors.exp: NTC thermistor: resistance decreases with temperature. Very high sensitivity (large dR/dT). Used for motor winding temperature protection (embedded thermistor), refrigeration control. Less accurate/stable than PT100 over wide range.

T07_Control_PLC.exp: PLC: industrial computer for automation. Inputs: sensors/switches. Processing: ladder logic/function blocks. Outputs: actuators/motors. Ruggedised for industrial environments.

T07_Control_PLC.a: Graphical programming language for PLCs using relay logic symbols (contacts, coils) on 'rungs'
opts: Graphical programming language for PLCs using relay logic symbols (contacts, coils) on 'rungs'
T07_Control_PLC.exp: Ladder logic: represents relay logic circuits. Normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC) contacts, coils, timers, counters. PLC scans from top-left to bottom-right, input to output.

T07_Control_PLC.a: Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition — monitors and controls distributed processes
opts: Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition — monitors and controls distributed processes
T07_Control_PLC.exp: SCADA: collects data from PLCs/RTUs via communication networks, displays on HMI, logs data, allows remote control. Used in ship automation: engine room monitoring, ballast control, cargo systems.

T07_Control_PLC.a: Proportional-Integral-Derivative — continuous control action based on error, error integral, and error derivative
opts: Proportional-Integral-Derivative — continuous control action based on error, error integral, and error derivative
T07_Control_PLC.exp: P: corrects in proportion to error. I: eliminates steady-state error (integrates over time). D: anticipates future error (rate of change). Tuned for stable, accurate process control.

T07_Control_PLC.q: What is 'proportional band' (P gain) in a controller?
T07_Control_PLC.a: Range of error over which controller output changes from 0% to 100% — wider band = less aggressive action
opts: Range of error over which controller output changes from 0% to 100% — wider band = less aggressive action
T07_Control_PLC.exp: Narrow P band: more aggressive response, may cause oscillation (hunting). Wide P band: stable but offset remains. P alone always has offset — needs I to eliminate.

T07_Control_PLC.q: What is 'integral action' in a PID controller?
T07_Control_PLC.a: Eliminates steady-state offset by integrating error over time and increasing output until error=0
opts: Eliminates steady-state offset by integrating error over time and increasing output until error=0
T07_Control_PLC.exp: Integral (reset): continuously increases/decreases output as long as error exists. Too much I: slow oscillation (integral windup). Reset time (Ti): time to repeat proportional action.

T07_Control_PLC.q: What is 'derivative action' in a PID?
T07_Control_PLC.a: Anticipates future error by responding to rate of change — provides damping, reduces overshoot
opts: Anticipates future error by responding to rate of change — provides damping, reduces overshoot
T07_Control_PLC.exp: Derivative (D): D output = Td × d(error)/dt. Provides damping — like a shock absorber. Too much D: amplifies noise, causes instability. Often filtered (PD with derivative filter).

T07_Control_PLC.q: What is 'hunting' in a control system?
T07_Control_PLC.a: Oscillation around setpoint due to excessive proportional or integral action
opts: Oscillation around setpoint due to excessive proportional or integral action
T07_Control_PLC.exp: Hunting: controller overshoots, corrects too hard, overshoots other way — cyclic oscillation. Fix: reduce P gain, increase Ti, add D action, or use manual tuning.

T07_Control_PLC.a: Varying the duty cycle (on/off ratio) of a switching signal to control average power or voltage
opts: Varying the duty cycle (on/off ratio) of a switching signal to control average power or voltage
T07_Control_PLC.exp: PWM: 50% duty cycle = 50% average voltage/power. Used in VFDs (motor speed), battery chargers, DC drives, LED dimming. High efficiency as switch is either fully on or fully off (no resistive losses).

T07_Control_PLC.a: Engine room automation, ballast control, cargo handling, steering gear, fire detection, power management
opts: Engine room automation, ballast control, cargo handling, steering gear, fire detection, power management
T07_Control_PLC.exp: PLCs are everywhere in modern ships: main engine control, boiler control, ballast water treatment, deck machinery, HVAC, fire detection system logic, main switchboard PMS.

T07_Control_PLC.q: What is the difference between analog and digital I/O?
T07_Control_PLC.a: Analog: continuous range (0-10V, 4-20mA); Digital: on/off (0V or 24V), binary signals
opts: Analog: continuous range (0-10V, 4-20mA); Digital: on/off (0V or 24V), binary signals
T07_Control_PLC.exp: Analog inputs: pressure transmitters, temperature sensors. Digital inputs: limit switches, pushbuttons, relay contacts. Analog outputs: control valves, VFD speed reference. Digital outputs: motor starters, solenoids.

T07_Control_PLC.q: What is a DCS (Distributed Control System)?
T07_Control_PLC.a: Control system with multiple distributed controllers networked together — more complex than single PLC
opts: Control system with multiple distributed controllers networked together — more complex than single PLC
T07_Control_PLC.exp: DCS: large plants — controllers distributed near equipment, connected by network to central HMI. Redundant controllers, high reliability. Used in large vessels, offshore platforms, LNG terminals.

T07_Control_PLC.a: Serial communication protocol widely used in industrial PLCs and instruments
opts: Serial communication protocol widely used in industrial PLCs and instruments
T07_Control_PLC.exp: Modbus RTU/ASCII: simple master-slave protocol. RS-485 physical layer. Widely supported by sensors, PLCs, drives, meters. Modbus TCP: same over Ethernet. Slow but reliable and universal.

T07_Control_PLC.q: What is a 'watchdog timer' in a PLC?
T07_Control_PLC.a: Timer that resets the PLC to safe state if program execution hangs or takes too long
opts: Timer that resets the PLC to safe state if program execution hangs or takes too long
T07_Control_PLC.exp: Watchdog: program must 'kick' (reset) the timer every scan cycle. If program hangs (software fault), watchdog expires and forces safe shutdown or restart. Safety critical.

T07_Control_PLC.q: What is 'scan time' in a PLC?
T07_Control_PLC.a: Time for PLC to read all inputs, execute program logic, and update all outputs — typically 1–100ms
opts: Time for PLC to read all inputs, execute program logic, and update all outputs — typically 1–100ms
T07_Control_PLC.exp: Scan time depends on program size and I/O count. For fast processes (servo control), need <1ms scan. For slow processes (temperature control), 100ms is fine. Critical for safety response times.

T08_Electronics.a: Material with conductivity between conductor and insulator — conductivity controlled by doping or voltage
opts: Material with conductivity between conductor and insulator — conductivity controlled by doping or voltage
T08_Electronics.exp: Semiconductors (silicon, germanium): intrinsic (pure) or doped (N-type: extra electrons, P-type: holes). Basis of diodes, transistors, thyristors, integrated circuits.

T08_Electronics.q: What is a P-N junction diode?
T08_Electronics.a: Two semiconductor layers (P and N) forming junction — allows current in one direction only (forward bias)
opts: Two semiconductor layers (P and N) forming junction — allows current in one direction only (forward bias)
T08_Electronics.exp: Forward bias (P+, N-): current flows, ~0.6V drop (silicon). Reverse bias: no current (depletion layer). Used for rectification, protection, signal detection.

T08_Electronics.a: Diode that conducts in reverse at precise 'breakdown' voltage — used as voltage reference/regulator
opts: Diode that conducts in reverse at precise 'breakdown' voltage — used as voltage reference/regulator
T08_Electronics.exp: Zener: maintains constant voltage across it when reverse current varies. Used in AVR reference circuits, power supply voltage regulation, protection circuits.

T08_Electronics.a: Silicon Controlled Rectifier — triggered on by gate pulse, conducts until current falls below holding current
opts: Silicon Controlled Rectifier — triggered on by gate pulse, conducts until current falls below holding current
T08_Electronics.exp: SCR: 4-layer PNPN device. Gate triggers conduction. Used in high power control: AC drives, DC drives, soft starters, rectifiers. Requires forced commutation in DC circuits.

T08_Electronics.a: Bidirectional thyristor — conducts in both directions when triggered by gate
opts: Bidirectional thyristor — conducts in both directions when triggered by gate
T08_Electronics.exp: TRIAC: two SCRs in anti-parallel. Used in AC power control: light dimmers, soft starters, motor speed control. Triggered each half-cycle.

T08_Electronics.a: Three-layer semiconductor device (NPN or PNP) — base current controls collector-emitter current (amplifier or switch)
opts: Three-layer semiconductor device (NPN or PNP) — base current controls collector-emitter current (amplifier or switch)
T08_Electronics.exp: BJT: IC = hFE × IB. Small base current controls large collector current. Used as: switch (digital circuits), amplifier (analog circuits). Replaced largely by MOSFETs for power applications.

T08_Electronics.a: Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor — voltage-controlled device, high speed switching
opts: Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor — voltage-controlled device, high speed switching
T08_Electronics.exp: MOSFET: gate voltage controls drain-source current. No gate current needed (voltage controlled). Fast switching — used in VFDs, switch-mode power supplies, inverters. IGBT combines MOSFET and BJT advantages.

T08_Electronics.a: Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor — combines MOSFET gate control with BJT high current capacity
opts: Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor — combines MOSFET gate control with BJT high current capacity
T08_Electronics.exp: IGBT: dominant in modern VFDs and inverters. High voltage (up to 6.5kV), high current, fast switching, low gate drive power. Used in all modern marine variable speed drives.

T08_Electronics.q: What is a full-wave bridge rectifier?
T08_Electronics.a: Four diodes in bridge configuration converting full AC cycle to pulsating DC
opts: Four diodes in bridge configuration converting full AC cycle to pulsating DC
T08_Electronics.exp: Bridge rectifier: uses both half-cycles of AC. Output: DC with ripple at 2× supply frequency. Smoothed by capacitor filter. Used in battery chargers, DC power supplies, VFD front-end.

T08_Electronics.q: What is an inverter in power electronics?
T08_Electronics.a: Converts DC to AC at desired frequency and voltage — used in UPS and VFD output stages
opts: Converts DC to AC at desired frequency and voltage — used in UPS and VFD output stages
T08_Electronics.exp: VFD: Rectifier (AC→DC) → DC link → Inverter (DC→variable AC). Inverter uses IGBTs with PWM control to produce sinusoidal output at desired frequency (0–120Hz+).

T08_Electronics.q: What is a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply)?
T08_Electronics.a: Provides continuous power during mains failure — battery backed, often with inverter for pure sine output
opts: Provides continuous power during mains failure — battery backed, often with inverter for pure sine output
T08_Electronics.exp: UPS: online (always through inverter), offline (switches on mains failure), or line-interactive. Used for navigation equipment, computers, emergency systems requiring continuous power.

T08_Electronics.a: High gain differential amplifier IC — foundation of analog signal processing circuits
opts: High gain differential amplifier IC — foundation of analog signal processing circuits
T08_Electronics.exp: Op-amp: very high gain (~100,000), high input impedance, low output impedance. With feedback: accurate amplifier, comparator, integrator, differentiator, filter. Used in sensor signal conditioning.

T08_Electronics.a: RC oscillator using three RC stages to produce 180° phase shift, providing positive feedback at one frequency
opts: RC oscillator using three RC stages to produce 180° phase shift, providing positive feedback at one frequency
T08_Electronics.exp: RC phase-shift oscillator: each RC stage contributes 60° phase shift. Three stages = 180°. Combined with 180° from inverting amplifier = 360° total = positive feedback at specific frequency. Produces sine wave.

T08_Electronics.q: What is the condition for sustained oscillations in a feedback circuit?
T08_Electronics.a: Barkhausen criterion: loop gain = 1 and total phase shift = 0° (or 360°)
opts: Barkhausen criterion: loop gain = 1 and total phase shift = 0° (or 360°)
T08_Electronics.exp: Barkhausen: Aβ = 1 (gain × feedback factor) and ∠Aβ = 0°. If Aβ > 1: oscillations grow. If Aβ < 1: oscillations decay. Self-sustaining at exactly Aβ = 1.

T08_Electronics.q: What is a transistor amplifier and what affects its frequency response?
T08_Electronics.a: Amplifies AC signals; frequency response limited at low end by coupling capacitors, at high end by transistor fT
opts: Amplifies AC signals; frequency response limited at low end by coupling capacitors, at high end by transistor fT
T08_Electronics.exp: Low frequency: coupling/bypass capacitors have high reactance — gain drops. High frequency: transistor gain decreases above transition frequency (fT), plus stray capacitances cause bypass. Midband: maximum flat gain.

T08_Electronics.q: What is a printed circuit board (PCB) and how should it be maintained?
T08_Electronics.a: Insulating board with copper tracks connecting components; maintenance: clean, check for dry joints, corrosion, heat damage
opts: Insulating board with copper tracks connecting components; maintenance: clean, check for dry joints, corrosion, heat damage
T08_Electronics.exp: PCB maintenance: inspect under magnification. Dry solder joints appear dull/cracked — resolder. Corrosion on tracks: marine humidity. Clean with isopropyl alcohol. Handle with ESD precautions.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What SOLAS requirement governs steering gear?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: SOLAS II-1/29: two independent steering gear systems, each capable of putting rudder hard-over to hard-over in 28 seconds
opts: SOLAS II-1/29: two independent steering gear systems, each capable of putting rudder hard-over to hard-over in 28 seconds
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Steering gear: 28 seconds hard-over to hard-over (35° each side) for ships >70,000 DWT. Two power units, each capable of operating independently. Power units must start automatically on power failure.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What are the electrical requirements for steering gear per SOLAS?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: Two independent power supplies from main switchboard, auto-changeover on failure of one supply
opts: Two independent power supplies from main switchboard, auto-changeover on failure of one supply
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: SOLAS II-1/29.14: two feeder circuits from MSB, capable of carrying full load independently. Auto-transfer within 45 seconds. Bridge alarm for steering gear failure.

T09_ShipMachinery.a: Transversely mounted propeller in tunnel through ship's bow for harbour manoeuvring
opts: Transversely mounted propeller in tunnel through ship's bow for harbour manoeuvring
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Bow thruster: controllable pitch propeller or fixed pitch with reversible motor. Motor typically: cage induction motor with DOL or soft start. Speed limitation: typically not used above 8 knots.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What is the purpose of the 'sequential start' after blackout?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: Prevents overloading restored generator by starting essential motors one at a time with time delays
opts: Prevents overloading restored generator by starting essential motors one at a time with time delays
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Sequential start: after blackout recovery, motors restart in priority order with time delays (typically 3–30 seconds between groups). Prevents all motors starting simultaneously = massive current inrush = possible blackout repeat.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What type of motor drives a purifier (separator)?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: High-speed AC induction motor with soft start or DOL, typically 3000 RPM on 50Hz (4-pole, 2-pole or via belt/coupling)
opts: High-speed AC induction motor with soft start or DOL, typically 3000 RPM on 50Hz (4-pole, 2-pole or via belt/coupling)
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Alfa Laval/Westfalia separators: typically 2-pole or 4-pole induction motor driving bowl via gearbox or direct belt. High inertia start — may need extended start time setting on overload relay.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What is the electrical supply to a deck crane?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: 440V 3-phase, typically through slip rings for slewing; motors for hoisting, luffing, slewing
opts: 440V 3-phase, typically through slip rings for slewing; motors for hoisting, slewing, luffing
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Crane motors: typically Ward Leonard or VVVF drives for speed control. Multiple motors: hoist, luff (boom angle), slew (rotation), travel. Slip rings provide power to rotating structure.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What safety devices are fitted on deck cranes?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: Overload limiter, hook upper/lower limit, slew limit, anemometer trip, crane control isolation
opts: Overload limiter, hook upper/lower limit, slew limit, anemometer trip, crane control isolation
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Crane safeties: SWL indicator, hook limit switches (up/down), boom limit switches, wind speed cut-off (anemometer), E-stop, mechanical brakes on all drives (fail-safe: apply on power loss).

T09_ShipMachinery.a: Deck machinery for raising/lowering anchor — motorised cable lifter and warping drums
opts: Deck machinery for raising/lowering anchor — motorised cable lifter and warping drums
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Windlass motor: typically 440V 3-phase induction motor with DOL or star-delta starting. High torque required. Mechanical band brake as holding device. Cable lifter: shaped to fit anchor chain.

T09_ShipMachinery.a: Vertical axis warping drum for mooring lines
opts: Vertical axis warping drum for mooring lines
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Capstan: motor-driven vertical drum. Operator takes turns of rope around drum, controls tension by hand. Used for warping (pulling ship toward berth). Motor typically induction motor with star-delta start.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What is an incinerator and what electrical equipment does it have?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: Burns waste onboard; electrical: combustion air fan motor, fuel pump motor, ignition transformer, temperature control
opts: Burns waste onboard; electrical: combustion air fan motor, fuel pump motor, ignition transformer, temperature control
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Incinerator: MARPOL V/MARPOL I waste disposal. Electrical: fan, fuel pump, ignition system, PLC control, temperature sensors (pyrometer), interlocks (door, over-temp), safety valves.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What is an oily water separator (OWS)?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: Separates oil from bilge water; must achieve <15ppm before overboard discharge
opts: Separates oil from bilge water; must achieve <15ppm before overboard discharge
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: OWS: gravity/coalescer separation. Oil content monitor (OCM) fitted in discharge line — must show <15ppm (MARPOL Annex I). OCM with 3-way valve — diverts to bilge if >15ppm. ORB entries required.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What types of motors are used in steering gear?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: AC induction motors (usually two motors per pump unit) or hydraulic pump motors
opts: AC induction motors (usually two motors per pump unit) or hydraulic pump motors
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Steering gear pump motors: typically DOL or soft start. Two motor/pump units per SOLAS requirement. Each capable of independent operation. Power unit changeover: automatic on failure or manual.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What is the purpose of a mooring winch auto-tension feature?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: Automatically pays out or hauls in line to maintain constant tension despite tidal/load changes
opts: Automatically pays out or hauls in line to maintain constant tension despite tidal/load changes
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: Auto-tension: VFD-controlled motor or hydraulic system maintains preset tension. Reduces manual monitoring. Risk: if set too high, excessive load on mooring line and bitts.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What check is done on steering gear before departure?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: Test both systems: hard-over to hard-over, check hydraulic level, check feedback, check bridge/ECR communication
opts: Test both systems: hard-over to hard-over, check hydraulic level, check feedback, check bridge/ECR communication
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: SOLAS II-1/26.4: steering gear test required within 12 hours before departure. Record in logbook: persons responsible, test results, time. Check: rudder response, communication, rudder angle indicator.

T09_ShipMachinery.q: What is 'Pulse Width Modulation' applied to propulsion control?
T09_ShipMachinery.a: Varies the on/off duty cycle of power switches to control average voltage/torque to propulsion motors
opts: Varies the on/off duty cycle of power switches to control average voltage/torque to propulsion motors
T09_ShipMachinery.exp: PWM in propulsion VFDs: IGBT switches at high frequency (2–16kHz), varying pulse width to synthesise desired sinusoidal voltage at desired frequency. Enables smooth, efficient speed control.

T10_ICCP.exp: ICCP: system that applies controlled DC current to ship's hull to prevent corrosion. Counteracts electrochemical corrosion by making hull cathodic (negative electrode).

T10_ICCP.a: Technique to prevent metal corrosion by making it the cathode of an electrochemical cell
opts: Technique to prevent metal corrosion by making it the cathode of an electrochemical cell
T10_ICCP.exp: Corrosion: anode dissolves (oxidation). Cathodic protection: supply electrons to make metal cathode → no dissolution. Either sacrificial anode (zinc corrodes instead) or impressed current (external DC).

T10_ICCP.q: What material is typically used for ICCP anodes?
T10_ICCP.a: Platinised titanium or mixed metal oxide (MMO) coated titanium
opts: Platinised titanium or mixed metal oxide (MMO) coated titanium
T10_ICCP.exp: ICCP anodes: inert (do not dissolve). Platinised titanium, MMO titanium. Mounted on hull in insulated fairing. Last many years without replacement.

T10_ICCP.q: What is a reference electrode in ICCP?
T10_ICCP.a: Measures hull potential to provide feedback to control unit — ensures correct protection level
opts: Measures hull potential to provide feedback to control unit — ensures correct protection level
T10_ICCP.exp: Reference electrode: measures potential of hull vs seawater. Control unit compares to setpoint (typically -800 to -1050 mV vs Ag/AgCl), adjusts current output. Silver/silver chloride (Ag/AgCl) or zinc electrodes used.

T10_ICCP.q: What is the target protection potential for a steel ship hull?
T10_ICCP.a: Typically -800 to -1050 mV vs Ag/AgCl reference electrode
opts: Typically -800 to -1050 mV vs Ag/AgCl reference electrode
T10_ICCP.exp: Protective range: -800 mV minimum (below this, corrosion occurs). -1050 mV maximum (more negative = hydrogen evolution, paint damage). Controlled automatically by ICCP unit.

T10_ICCP.a: Block of active metal (zinc, aluminium, or magnesium) that corrodes preferentially, protecting attached steel
opts: Block of active metal (zinc, aluminium, or magnesium) that corrodes preferentially, protecting attached steel
T10_ICCP.exp: Sacrificial anodes: zinc most common in seawater. More active (negative potential) than steel — become anode in galvanic cell, corrode and protect steel. Replace in drydock when 50% consumed.

T10_ICCP.q: Why are ICCP systems switched off during drydock?
T10_ICCP.a: Hull exposed to air — no electrolyte, no protection needed; impressed current could damage paint and propeller shaft seals
opts: Hull exposed to air — no electrolyte, no protection needed; impressed current could damage paint and propeller shaft seals
T10_ICCP.exp: ICCP in drydock: must be switched off. Hull in air = no circuit. Stray current could damage shaft seals, propeller bearings. Sacrificial anodes replaced during drydock.

T10_ICCP.q: What is the purpose of shaft earthing (shaft grounding)?
T10_ICCP.a: Prevents galvanic corrosion of propeller shaft bearings by providing low-resistance path for stray currents
opts: Prevents galvanic corrosion of propeller shaft bearings by providing low-resistance path for stray currents
T10_ICCP.exp: Shaft grounding: brush on rotating shaft provides electrical continuity to hull. Without it, ICCP stray currents flow through shaft bearings — electrolytic corrosion. Also prevents shaft-induced bearing damage.

T10_ICCP.q: How does the ICCP control unit work?
T10_ICCP.a: Monitors reference electrode potential, adjusts DC output current to maintain hull at set protection potential
opts: Monitors reference electrode potential, adjusts DC output current to maintain hull at set protection potential
T10_ICCP.exp: Control loop: reference electrode → potential measurement → compare to setpoint → error signal → adjust rectifier DC output → anode current changes → hull potential changes → feedback.

T10_ICCP.q: Why must zinc anodes not be used in freshwater tanks?
T10_ICCP.a: Zinc oxides form insulating layer in fresh water — aluminium anodes preferred for tanks and freshwater
opts: Zinc oxides form insulating layer in fresh water — aluminium anodes preferred for tanks and freshwater
T10_ICCP.exp: In seawater: zinc oxide soluble, zinc remains active. In freshwater: zinc oxide builds up, passivates anode. Use aluminium (Al-In-Zn alloy) for tanks, freshwater. Magnesium for very low conductivity water.

T11_PowerFactor.a: Ratio of real power (kW) to apparent power (kVA) — cos φ where φ is angle between voltage and current
opts: Ratio of real power (kW) to apparent power (kVA) — cos φ where φ is angle between voltage and current
T11_PowerFactor.exp: PF = kW/kVA = cos φ. Ranges 0–1. Unity PF (1.0): current and voltage in phase, all power useful. Lagging PF: inductive loads. Leading PF: capacitive loads.

T11_PowerFactor.q: Why is low power factor harmful?
T11_PowerFactor.a: Higher current for same power → more cable/generator heating, lower efficiency, higher losses
opts: Higher current for same power → more cable/generator heating, lower efficiency, higher losses
T11_PowerFactor.exp: At PF 0.5: need 2× current for same kW as at PF 1.0. All those extra amps heat cables, generators, transformers without doing useful work. Generator rated in kVA — at low PF, kW output is much less.

T11_PowerFactor.q: How are capacitors used for power factor correction?
T11_PowerFactor.a: Capacitors supply reactive current locally, reducing reactive current from generator, improving system PF
opts: Capacitors supply reactive current locally, reducing reactive current from generator, improving system PF
T11_PowerFactor.exp: Capacitor bank: connected in parallel with inductive loads. Leading reactive current from capacitors cancels lagging reactive current from motors. Net reactive demand on generator reduced → better PF.

T11_PowerFactor.a: Reactive power (kilovolt-ampere reactive) — power oscillating between source and reactive loads, doing no work
opts: Reactive power (kilovolt-ampere reactive) — power oscillating between source and reactive loads, doing no work
T11_PowerFactor.exp: kVAR = kVA × sin φ. The reactive component. Inductive loads absorb kVAR (lagging). Capacitors supply kVAR (leading). Synchronous generators or motors can supply/absorb kVAR by excitation control.

T11_PowerFactor.a: Right triangle: kW (horizontal), kVAR (vertical), kVA (hypotenuse) — PF = kW/kVA
opts: Right triangle: kW (horizontal), kVAR (vertical), kVA (hypotenuse) — PF = kW/kVA
T11_PowerFactor.exp: Power triangle: kVA² = kW² + kVAR². PF = cos(arctan(kVAR/kW)). Adding capacitor kVAR reduces net kVAR → smaller angle → higher PF → smaller kVA for same kW.

T11_PowerFactor.q: How can a synchronous motor improve power factor?
T11_PowerFactor.a: By over-exciting the motor field, it draws leading current which compensates for lagging current of other loads
opts: By over-exciting the motor field, it draws leading current which compensates for lagging current of other loads
T11_PowerFactor.exp: Synchronous capacitor (synchronous motor running unloaded): over-excited → draws leading current → improves system PF. More controllable than fixed capacitor banks. Also used on shore supplies.

T11_PowerFactor.a: PF = 1.0 — current and voltage perfectly in phase, all apparent power is real power
opts: PF = 1.0 — current and voltage perfectly in phase, all apparent power is real power
T11_PowerFactor.exp: Unity PF: ideal but rarely achieved in practice. Most marine loads are inductive (PF 0.7–0.9 lagging). Target system PF: 0.8–0.9 lagging. Running generators at very low PF is inefficient.

T11_PowerFactor.q: What measurement instruments are needed to calculate power factor?
T11_PowerFactor.a: Wattmeter (kW) and VA meter (kVA), or kVAR meter, or power factor meter directly
opts: Wattmeter (kW) and VA meter (kVA), or kVAR meter, or power factor meter directly
T11_PowerFactor.exp: PF = kW/kVA. Measure kW with wattmeter (accounts for phase angle). Measure apparent power kVA = V × I. PF = W/(VI). Power analyzers measure all components simultaneously.

T11_PowerFactor.q: What is the effect of capacitor bank on voltage?
T11_PowerFactor.a: If over-compensated (too much capacitance), voltage rises above nominal — can damage equipment
opts: If over-compensated (too much capacitance), voltage rises above nominal — can damage equipment
T11_PowerFactor.exp: Capacitor banks supply reactive current into the system. This current through line impedance raises voltage. Over-compensation → overvoltage. AVR of generator will reduce excitation in response.

T11_PowerFactor.q: In a 3-phase system, how are capacitors connected for PF correction?
T11_PowerFactor.a: Star (Y) or delta (Δ) connection across phases — delta preferred for 3-phase correction (higher voltage across each cap)
opts: Star (Y) or delta (Δ) connection across phases — delta preferred for 3-phase correction (higher voltage across each cap)
T11_PowerFactor.exp: Delta connection: each capacitor sees full line voltage. Star: each capacitor sees line/√3 voltage (less reactive power per capacitor). Both used — delta more compact for same kVAR.

T12_Cables.exp: XLPE: thermoset insulation (cross-linked = can't melt). Better high temperature performance than PVC. Used for 11kV and 6.6kV cables on ships.

T12_Cables.q: What does SWA stand for in cable specification?
T12_Cables.a: Steel Wire Armoured — mechanical protection for cable
opts: Steel Wire Armoured — mechanical protection for cable
T12_Cables.exp: SWA: steel wires laid over cable core, providing mechanical protection and earthing continuity. Used where cable exposed to physical damage. Also provides earth return path.

T12_Cables.q: What is the minimum insulation resistance for a cable?
T12_Cables.a: 1 MΩ minimum — measured with 500V megger for 440V cables
opts: 1 MΩ minimum — measured with 500V megger for 440V cables
T12_Cables.exp: Cable IR test: pre-commission and periodic. Wet insulation, mechanical damage, contamination reduce IR. Below 1 MΩ: investigate and repair before energising.

T12_Cables.a: Fitting that provides mechanical support, earthing, and watertight seal where cable enters enclosure
opts: Fitting that provides mechanical support, earthing, and watertight seal where cable enters enclosure
T12_Cables.exp: Gland types: A1 (unarmoured), A2 (armoured), BW (armoured with earth continuity). Marine glands: IP67/IP68 rated for watertight bulkhead penetrations. Correct gland size critical.

T12_Cables.a: Maximum continuous current the cable can carry without exceeding conductor temperature limit
opts: Maximum continuous current the cable can carry without exceeding conductor temperature limit
T12_Cables.exp: Ampacity depends on: conductor size (mm²), insulation type, ambient temperature, grouping derating, installation method. Undersized cables overheat → insulation damage → fire.

T12_Cables.q: What is the derating factor for grouped cables?
T12_Cables.a: Reduction in current capacity when cables are bunched together — less heat dissipation
opts: Reduction in current capacity when cables are bunched together — less heat dissipation
T12_Cables.exp: Grouped cables: each cable's heat adds to others. Derating factors: 2 cables = 0.8, 4 cables = 0.7, 6 cables = 0.57. Space cables where possible on high-current circuits.

T12_Cables.q: What type of cable is required for essential services (fire pumps, emergency lights)?
T12_Cables.a: Fire resistant cable — maintains circuit integrity during fire (typically IEC 60331 rated)
opts: Fire resistant cable — maintains circuit integrity during fire (typically IEC 60331 rated)
T12_Cables.exp: SOLAS: fire-resistant cables for escape lighting, emergency fire pumps, public address, emergency steering. Cable must maintain operation for minimum 30 minutes in fire.

T12_Cables.q: What is the purpose of cable trays and ladders?
T12_Cables.a: Support and route cables, allow air circulation for cooling, allow inspection and modification
opts: Support and route cables, allow air circulation for cooling, allow inspection and modification
T12_Cables.exp: Cable trays: perforated or ladder type. Allow airflow (important for heat dissipation). Cables must be secured at appropriate intervals. Earthed tray provides mechanical protection and EMC shielding.

T12_Cables.q: What checks are done during cable inspection?
T12_Cables.a: Check for mechanical damage, chafing, correct glands, IR values, overheating signs, proper support
opts: Check for mechanical damage, chafing, correct glands, IR values, overheating signs, proper support
T12_Cables.exp: Cable inspection: trace route for damage, check gland integrity, look for heat discolouration, measure IR periodically, thermal imaging under load to detect loose connections or overloaded cables.

T12_Cables.a: Floating cable for rescue boats, lifeboats — remains on surface when deployed
opts: Cable that floats on water during installation
Floating cable for rescue boats, lifeboats — remains on surface when deployed
T12_Cables.exp: Buoyant cable: used for lifeboat electrical connections, rescue boat launch equipment. Low density foam insulation makes it float. Required by SOLAS for lifeboat hook/painter systems.

T12_Cables.q: What cable size is typically used for 440V motor feeders?
T12_Cables.a: Depends on motor kW and distance; commonly 2.5mm² to 95mm² — calculated from ampacity and voltage drop
opts: Depends on motor kW and distance; commonly 2.5mm² to 95mm² — calculated from ampacity and voltage drop
T12_Cables.exp: Cable sizing: step 1 - calculate FLC from motor kW/voltage/PF. Step 2 - select cable with ampacity ≥ FLC. Step 3 - check voltage drop ≤3%. Step 4 - check short circuit rating.

T12_Cables.q: What is the purpose of earthing cables?
T12_Cables.a: Provides low-impedance return path for fault current, enabling protection to operate and preventing dangerous touch voltages
opts: Provides low-impedance return path for fault current, enabling protection to operate and preventing dangerous touch voltages
T12_Cables.exp: Earth cable: must carry full fault current until protection operates. Sized per calculated fault current and protection clearing time. Typically green/yellow or separate earth conductor.

T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Global Maritime Distress and Safety System — integrated communications for distress, safety, and routine communications
opts: Global Maritime Distress and Safety System — integrated communications for distress, safety, and routine communications
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: GMDSS: SOLAS IV requirement. Equipment varies by sea area (A1–A4). Includes: VHF DSC, MF/HF DSC, EPIRB, SART, Navtex, Inmarsat. Automatic distress alerting.

T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon — automatically activates and transmits on 406MHz to COSPAS-SARSAT satellite
opts: Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon — automatically activates and transmits on 406MHz to COSPAS-SARSAT satellite
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: EPIRB: Category 1 (auto-activated by HRU at 4m depth) or Category 2 (manual). Transmits ship ID, position to COSPAS-SARSAT satellites → forwarded to MRCC within minutes.

T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Search And Rescue Transponder — responds to 9GHz radar transmission, showing position on rescuer's radar
opts: Search And Rescue Transponder — responds to 9GHz radar transmission, showing position on rescuer's radar
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: SART: activated by survivors in lifeboat/water. When interrogated by 9GHz radar, responds with series of blips extending radially on radar display. Indicates survivor position to rescuers.

T13_BridgeEquip1.q: What frequency does EPIRB transmit on?
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: 406 MHz: digital, carries ship ID (MMSI), position (if GPS-linked), processed by COSPAS-SARSAT. 121.5 MHz: homing signal for SAR aircraft. No longer processed by satellites.

T13_BridgeEquip1.q: What is a gyrocompass and how does it work?
T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Uses gyroscope principle (gyroscope axis aligns with Earth's rotation axis, pointing to true north) and pendulous system
opts: Uses gyroscope principle (gyroscope axis aligns with Earth's rotation axis, pointing to true north) and pendulous system
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: Gyrocompass: rapidly spinning gyroscope. Due to Earth's rotation and gravity correction (pendulous), gyro axis settles pointing to true (geographic) north. Not affected by ship's magnetic field.

T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Automated system for broadcast of navigational warnings, meteorological forecasts and urgent maritime information on 518kHz
opts: Automated system for broadcast of navigational warnings, meteorological forecasts and urgent maritime information on 518kHz
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: NAVTEX: narrow band direct printing (NBDP). Receiver automatically prints relevant messages. Each station/message type has identity code. Ship can select which stations/message types to receive.

T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Automatic Identification System — transponder broadcasting ship's identity, position, course, speed to other ships and VTS
opts: Automatic Identification System — transponder broadcasting ship's identity, position, course, speed to other ships and VTS
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: AIS: VHF (161.975 MHz and 162.025 MHz), TDMA. Class A (SOLAS ships): broadcasts every 2–10 seconds. Data: MMSI, name, type, position, COG, SOG, destination. Mandatory SOLAS V/19.

T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Electronic Chart Display and Information System — digital chart display integrated with position, AIS, radar overlay
opts: Electronic Chart Display and Information System — digital chart display integrated with position, AIS, radar overlay
Electronic Control and Display for Instruments
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: ECDIS: replaces paper charts when type-approved with updated ENCs (Electronic Navigational Charts). SOLAS V/19: mandatory for new SOLAS ships. Safety contour, anti-grounding alarm, route monitoring.

T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Long Range Identification and Tracking — reports ship position to flag state every 6 hours via satellite
opts: Long Range Identification and Tracking — reports ship position to flag state every 6 hours via satellite
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: LRIT: SOLAS V/19-1 (2008). Ships transmit position to LRIT Data Centre every 6 hours. Flag state and port state (when within 1000nm) can request more frequent reports. Administered by IMO.

T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Digital Selective Calling on VHF — digital distress alert on channel 70, includes ship position if GPS connected
opts: Very High Frequency Direct Ship Call
Digital Selective Calling on VHF — digital distress alert on channel 70, includes ship position if GPS connected
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: DSC (Digital Selective Calling): automated digital distress signal sent on Ch 70 (VHF), 2187.5kHz (MF) or HF. Includes MMSI, nature of distress, position, time. Follow up with voice on Ch 16.

T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Measures water depth by sending acoustic pulse downward and timing the echo return
opts: Measures water depth by sending acoustic pulse downward and timing the echo return
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: Echo sounder: transducer emits ultrasonic pulse, timer starts. Echo from seabed returns — time × speed of sound /2 = depth. Speed of sound in water: ~1500 m/s (varies with temp, salinity).

T13_BridgeEquip1.q: What does GMDSS sea area A1 cover?
T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Within range of shore-based VHF station with DSC — typically 20–50 nautical miles from coast
opts: Within range of shore-based VHF station with DSC — typically 20–50 nautical miles from coast
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: Sea areas: A1 (VHF DSC range), A2 (MF DSC range, typically <400nm), A3 (Inmarsat coverage, within ~70° latitude), A4 (polar regions, outside A1-A3). Equipment carried depends on sea area of operation.

T13_BridgeEquip1.q: What is the purpose of a voyage data recorder (VDR)?
T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Records bridge data (audio, radar, position, speed, heading) for accident investigation
opts: Records bridge data (audio, radar, position, speed, heading) for accident investigation
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: VDR: SOLAS V/20. Mandatory for passenger ships and most cargo ships. Records last 12 hours: audio (bridge, VHF), radar, position, heading, speed, echo sounder, alarms, ECDIS. Survivable capsule.

T13_BridgeEquip1.q: What is the speed log and types?
T13_BridgeEquip1.a: Measures ship's speed through water; types: Doppler (acoustic), EM (electromagnetic), GPS (over ground)
opts: Measures ship's speed through water; types: Doppler (acoustic), EM (electromagnetic), GPS (over ground)
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: EM log: measures interaction between ship's hull movement and seawater using electromagnetic induction. Doppler log: measures forward and transverse speed. GPS gives speed over ground (not through water).

T13_BridgeEquip1.q: What is the magnetron in a radar?
T13_BridgeEquip1.a: High-power microwave oscillator that generates the radar transmission pulses at 3GHz (S-band) or 9GHz (X-band)
opts: High-power microwave oscillator that generates the radar transmission pulses at 3GHz (S-band) or 9GHz (X-band)
T13_BridgeEquip1.exp: Magnetron: cavity resonator with permanent magnet and high voltage. Generates GHz microwaves. High voltage (typically 15–50kV) required — serious shock hazard. Never open radar while transmitting.

T14_BridgeEquip2.a: Ship Security Alert System — silent distress alert to flag state without alerting pirates/hijackers
opts: Ship Security Alert System — silent distress alert to flag state without alerting pirates/hijackers
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: SSAS: SOLAS XI-2/6. Silent alert sent to flag state administration (no local alarm). Activated from two points on ship (bridge + one other). Notifies CSO (Company Security Officer) and flag state.

T14_BridgeEquip2.q: What is a VDR protected capsule?
T14_BridgeEquip2.a: Waterproof, fire-resistant capsule storing last 12 hours of VDR data, designed to survive sinking or fire
opts: Waterproof, fire-resistant capsule storing last 12 hours of VDR data, designed to survive sinking or fire
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: VDR capsule: float-free (releases at 4m depth), EPIRB-like location beacon, withstands fire (1100°C for 1 hour), impact, hydrostatic pressure. Orange colour, bright reflective tape.

T14_BridgeEquip2.a: System that automatically steers the ship to a set heading using gyrocompass feedback and rudder control
opts: System that automatically steers the ship to a set heading using gyrocompass feedback and rudder control
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: Autopilot: heading error → PID controller → rudder order → steering gear. Adaptive autopilots: learn ship response characteristics. Weather mode: reduces rudder activity in heavy weather to save fuel.

T14_BridgeEquip2.q: What is a window wiper on a bridge?
T14_BridgeEquip2.a: Electrical motor-driven rotating disc or blade that clears rain/spray from bridge windows
opts: Electrical motor-driven rotating disc or blade that clears rain/spray from bridge windows
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: Window wiper: heated glass (spinning disc type) or blade wiper. Motor types: shaded pole, PSC or small induction motor. Heated glass: electric heating element prevents condensation and ice.

T14_BridgeEquip2.q: What is a searchlight and its electrical supply?
T14_BridgeEquip2.a: High intensity directional light for signalling/navigation; typically 24V DC halogen or high-power LED
opts: High intensity directional light for signalling/navigation; typically 24V DC halogen or high-power LED
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: Searchlight: bridge wing mounted, remote or manual control. Traditional: 500W-1000W halogen. Modern: LED searchlights (lower power, longer life). Used for: man overboard, collision avoidance, signalling.

T14_BridgeEquip2.q: What are the SOLAS navigation light requirements?
T14_BridgeEquip2.a: Specific lights required based on vessel type, size, and situation: masthead, stern, side (port/starboard), anchor lights
opts: Specific lights required based on vessel type, size, and situation: masthead, stern, side (port/starboard), anchor lights
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: SOLAS V/Colregs: masthead (white, 225°), port (red, 112.5°), starboard (green, 112.5°), stern (white, 135°). Two-circuit supply required: automatic switchover on failure, alarm on bridge.

T14_BridgeEquip2.q: What is the purpose of a fog signal device?
T14_BridgeEquip2.a: Sound signal device for use in restricted visibility — electric bell, whistle, or horn
opts: Sound signal device for use in restricted visibility — electric bell, whistle, or horn
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: Colregs Rule 35: power-driven vessel underway in fog sounds one prolonged blast every 2 minutes. Equipment: electric or pneumatic horn/whistle. Automatic fog signalling systems available.

T14_BridgeEquip2.a: Networked combination of bridge equipment (radar, ECDIS, autopilot, AIS) sharing data on common displays
opts: Networked combination of bridge equipment (radar, ECDIS, autopilot, AIS) sharing data on common displays
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: IBS: equipment interoperability. ECDIS receives radar overlay, AIS targets, GPS. Autopilot receives heading from gyro, route from ECDIS. Reduces parallel workload, improves situational awareness.

T14_BridgeEquip2.q: What maintenance is done on bridge navigation equipment?
T14_BridgeEquip2.a: Annual calibration (gyro error), EPIRB/SART battery replacement, VDR capsule hydrotest, AIS transponder test
opts: Annual calibration (gyro error), EPIRB/SART battery replacement, VDR capsule hydrotest, AIS transponder test
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: Bridge equipment PM: EPIRB/SART battery/hydrostatic release expiry, VDR annual performance test, gyro error check, AIS transponder MMSI programming verification, navigation light test/record.

T14_BridgeEquip2.a: Maritime Mobile Service Identity — 9-digit number identifying vessel for DSC and AIS
opts: Maritime Mobile Service Identity — 9-digit number identifying vessel for DSC and AIS
T14_BridgeEquip2.exp: MMSI: unique vessel identifier. First 3 digits = MID (Maritime Identification Digit = country code). Programmed in all DSC, AIS, EPIRB equipment. Used by MRCC to identify distress vessel.

T15_FireFighting.a: International Code for Fire Safety Systems — specifies requirements for fixed fire fighting systems
opts: International Code for Fire Safety Systems — specifies requirements for fixed fire fighting systems
T15_FireFighting.exp: FSS Code (2000, amended): under SOLAS II-2. Specifies: CO2 systems, foam systems, sprinklers, fire detection, fixed pressure water spraying, halon alternatives.

T15_FireFighting.q: How does a CO2 fixed firefighting system work?
T15_FireFighting.a: CO2 released into space extinguishes fire by displacing oxygen (O2 reduced below ~14%)
opts: CO2 released into space extinguishes fire by displacing oxygen (O2 reduced below ~14%)
T15_FireFighting.exp: CO2: smothers fire by reducing oxygen. Concentration needed: 34–40% by volume. Fatal to humans at >9%. Two-stage release: pilot cylinder opens, time delay for evacuation, then main bank releases.

T15_FireFighting.q: What safety precautions before releasing CO2?
T15_FireFighting.a: Sound alarm, ensure all personnel evacuated, close ventilation, shut all openings, verify space is clear
opts: Sound alarm, ensure all personnel evacuated, close ventilation, shut all openings, verify space is clear
T15_FireFighting.exp: CO2 release procedure: 1) Evacuate and account for all persons 2) Sound CO2 alarm 3) Wait prescribed time 4) Close ventilation dampers 5) Close watertight doors 6) Release CO2. CO2 WILL kill if persons inside.

T15_FireFighting.q: What is a hi-fog/water mist system?
T15_FireFighting.a: Fine water spray system creating tiny droplets — extinguishes by cooling, displacing oxygen, steam inerting
opts: Fine water spray system creating tiny droplets — extinguishes by cooling, displacing oxygen, steam inerting
T15_FireFighting.exp: Hi-fog: droplets <100–400 microns. High surface area: efficient cooling. Minimum water use. Suitable for machinery spaces, accommodation. Low pressure (<25 bar) or high pressure (up to 200 bar).

T15_FireFighting.q: What type of fire extinguisher is used for electrical fires?
T15_FireFighting.a: CO2 or dry powder — NEVER water or foam on electrical fires
opts: CO2 or dry powder — NEVER water or foam on electrical fires
T15_FireFighting.exp: Electrical fires: water/foam = electrocution risk. CO2: clean, no residue, displaces oxygen, safe for electronics. Dry powder: effective but leaves residue (damages equipment). Halon 1301: banned (ozone depletion).

T15_FireFighting.q: What is the purpose of a fire damper?
T15_FireFighting.a: Automatically closes in ventilation duct on fire/smoke detection to prevent fire spread
opts: Automatically closes in ventilation duct on fire/smoke detection to prevent fire spread
T15_FireFighting.exp: Fire damper: fusible link (melts at ~70°C) or electrically operated. Closed to contain fire and smoke. SOLAS II-2/9: ventilation systems must have fire dampers at compartment boundaries.

T15_FireFighting.q: What is a foam firefighting system?
T15_FireFighting.a: Water-foam mixture creates blanket over burning fuel — smothers, cools and excludes oxygen
opts: Water-foam mixture creates blanket over burning fuel — smothers, cools and excludes oxygen
T15_FireFighting.exp: Foam types: AFFF (Aqueous Film Forming Foam), AR-AFFF (alcohol resistant), protein foam. Expansion ratio: low (5:1–20:1), medium (20:1–200:1), high expansion (>200:1). Used for class B fires (flammable liquids).

T15_FireFighting.q: What classes of fire are there?
T15_FireFighting.a: Class A: solid; B: flammable liquid; C: gas; D: metal; E: electrical; F: cooking oils
opts: Class A: solid; B: flammable liquid; C: gas; D: metal; E: electrical; F: cooking oils
T15_FireFighting.exp: Fire classes: A (wood, paper, textiles), B (petrol, oil, diesel), C (natural gas, LPG), D (metals: sodium, magnesium), E (electrical equipment), F (cooking oils). Extinguisher choice depends on class.

T15_FireFighting.q: What is a sprinkler system and where required?
T15_FireFighting.a: Automatic water spray system activating on heat; SOLAS II-2 requires on passenger ships, ro-ro ships, accommodation
opts: Automatic water spray system activating on heat; SOLAS II-2 requires on passenger ships, ro-ro ships, accommodation
T15_FireFighting.exp: Sprinkler head: glass bulb (red=68°C, yellow=79°C, green=93°C) breaks at rated temperature, releases water. Alarm activates on pressure drop. Pumped from dedicated tank or sea water via pump.

T15_FireFighting.q: What is the emergency fire pump and SOLAS requirement?
T15_FireFighting.a: Independent motor-driven pump providing fire main pressure when main fire pump fails; located outside machinery space
opts: Independent motor-driven pump providing fire main pressure when main fire pump fails; located outside machinery space
T15_FireFighting.exp: SOLAS II-2/10.2.2.4: emergency fire pump — independent of main machinery space, driven by separate motor with independent fuel supply, capable of delivering 2 jets. Mandatory on most SOLAS vessels.

T15_FireFighting.q: What is a fixed pressure water spraying system (SOLAS)?
T15_FireFighting.a: Fine water spray system protecting engine room machinery — activated manually on fire detection
opts: Fine water spray system protecting engine room machinery — activated manually on fire detection
T15_FireFighting.exp: PWSS (Pressure Water Spraying System): covers machinery space bilges, purifiers, engine casing — areas with Class B fire risk. Nozzles provide cone of spray. Actuated from outside machinery space.

T15_FireFighting.q: What is the SOLAS requirement for smoke detectors?
T15_FireFighting.a: SOLAS II-2/7: approved smoke detection and fire alarm system in crew accommodation, service spaces, control stations
opts: SOLAS II-2/7: approved smoke detection and fire alarm system in crew accommodation, service spaces, control stations
T15_FireFighting.exp: Smoke detectors: photoelectric (scatter light) or ionisation (alpha particle ionisation). Heat detectors: rate-of-rise or fixed temperature. Flame detectors: UV or IR sensing.

T15_FireFighting.q: What is the fire main system?
T15_FireFighting.a: System of pipes distributing seawater to fire hydrants throughout ship
opts: System of pipes distributing seawater to fire hydrants throughout ship
T15_FireFighting.exp: Fire main: continuously pressurised or capable of being quickly pressurised. Number and position of hydrants: SOLAS II-2/10. Hoses and nozzles at each hydrant (jet and spray pattern).

T15_FireFighting.a: Standard coupling for connecting shore fire main to ship's fire main — uniform size worldwide
opts: Standard coupling for connecting shore fire main to ship's fire main — uniform size worldwide
T15_FireFighting.exp: International shore connection (ISC): SOLAS II-2/10.2.1.7. Flange 178mm outside diameter, 4 bolts on 132mm PCD. Allows shore fire brigade to supply ship's fire main. Carried onboard.

T15_FireFighting.q: What fire protection is required in paint stores?
T15_FireFighting.a: CO2 or dry powder fixed system, fire-resistant construction, sprinkler or detection, no sources of ignition
opts: CO2 or dry powder fixed system, fire-resistant construction, sprinkler or detection, no sources of ignition
T15_FireFighting.exp: Paint store: high fire risk (flammable solvents). SOLAS: A-class boundaries, mechanical ventilation, CO2/dry powder. No electrical fittings inside except safe-type. Explosion-proof if in hazardous area.

T16_SOLAS.q: How many chapters does SOLAS have?
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS chapters: I (General), II-1 (Construction), II-2 (Fire), III (LSA), IV (Radio), V (Navigation), VI (Carriage of cargo), VII (Dangerous goods), VIII (Nuclear), IX (ISM), X (HSC), XI-1 (Safety measures), XI-2 (Security/ISPS), XII (Bulk carriers), XIV (Polar Code).

T16_SOLAS.q: What does SOLAS Chapter II-1 cover?
T16_SOLAS.a: Construction, stability, machinery and electrical installations
opts: Construction, stability, machinery and electrical installations
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS II-1: subdivision and damage stability, machinery installation (steering gear, bilge pumps), electrical installations (essential services, emergency sources of power).

T16_SOLAS.q: What does SOLAS Chapter II-2 cover?
T16_SOLAS.a: Fire protection, fire detection and fire extinction
opts: Fire protection, fire detection and fire extinction
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS II-2: structural fire protection, fire detection and alarm, suppression systems, escape routes, firefighting equipment, cargo ship safety construction certificate.

T16_SOLAS.q: What does SOLAS Chapter III cover?
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS III: lifeboat, rescue boat, liferaft, EPIRB, SART, distress signals, immersion suits, life jackets, ring lifebuoys. LSA Code gives detailed specifications.

T16_SOLAS.q: What does SOLAS Chapter IV cover?
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS IV: GMDSS requirements. VHF DSC, MF/HF, Inmarsat, EPIRB, SART, Navtex. Sea areas A1–A4. Radio watchkeeping, radio log, GMDSS certificates.

T16_SOLAS.q: What does SOLAS Chapter V cover?
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS V: navigational equipment (radar, ECDIS, AIS, VDR, echo sounder), bridge design, voyage planning, lookout duties, distress signals, dangerous ice reporting, Vessel Traffic Services.

T16_SOLAS.a: ISM Code — International Safety Management Code
opts: ISM Code — International Safety Management Code
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS IX incorporates ISM Code. Requires Safety Management System (SMS) for all SOLAS vessels. Documents, procedures, audits, non-conformities, DOC (Document of Compliance), SMC (Safety Management Certificate).

T16_SOLAS.q: What does SOLAS Chapter XI-2 cover?
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS XI-2: ISPS (International Ship and Port Facility Security) Code. Ship Security Plan (SSP), Ship Security Officer (SSO), security levels (1, 2, 3), SSAS, CSR (Continuous Synopsis Record).

T16_SOLAS.q: What is a Certificate of Class?
T16_SOLAS.a: Certificate issued by classification society confirming ship meets class rules for hull, machinery, and equipment
opts: Certificate issued by classification society confirming ship meets class rules for hull, machinery, and equipment
T16_SOLAS.exp: Class certificate: Class notation (e.g. +100A1 +LMC) indicates structural and machinery classification. Not statutory — but P&I clubs, insurers, charterers require it. Valid until next class survey.

T16_SOLAS.q: What is SOLAS Regulation V/26 on steering gear tests?
T16_SOLAS.a: Tests within 12 hours before departure, record in logbook
opts: Tests within 12 hours before departure, record in logbook
T16_SOLAS.exp: V/26.4: within 12 hours before departure, test: main and auxiliary steering gear, gyrocompass, magnetic compass, bridge control systems, rudder angle indicators, automatic/manual backup.

T16_SOLAS.q: What is the minimum lifeboat capacity required per SOLAS?
T16_SOLAS.a: Sufficient lifeboats on each side for 100% of persons — plus liferafts for 25% additional
opts: Sufficient lifeboats on each side for 100% of persons — plus liferafts for 25% additional
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS III/21: each side capable of carrying all persons. Total: 200% capacity in lifeboats. Plus: liferafts covering at least 25% (to allow for damage to lifeboats). Cargo ships: at least one rescue boat.

T16_SOLAS.q: What is the immersion suit performance requirement?
T16_SOLAS.a: Must allow donning in ≤2 minutes, maintain body heat, allow swimming, be visible (bright colour)
opts: Must allow donning in ≤2 minutes, maintain body heat, allow swimming, be visible (bright colour)
T16_SOLAS.exp: LSA Code Chapter 2: immersion suit — maintain body temperature <2°C drop in water 0–2°C for 6 hours. Donnable in 2 minutes with gloves. Righting in 5 seconds. Light and whistle.

T16_SOLAS.q: What is the SOLAS requirement for lifeboat launch?
T16_SOLAS.a: Must be capable of being launched and towed when ship is making headway up to 5 knots
opts: Must be capable of being launched and towed when ship is making headway up to 5 knots
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS III/31.1: free-fall lifeboats must be capable of being launched when ship is making headway up to 5 knots. Gravity davit systems: same requirement.

T16_SOLAS.q: What SOLAS certificates are required on a cargo ship?
T16_SOLAS.a: Safety Equipment Certificate, Safety Radio Certificate, Safety Construction Certificate, IOPP Certificate, Load Line Certificate, Safe Manning Document
opts: Safety Equipment Certificate, Safety Radio Certificate, Safety Construction Certificate, IOPP Certificate, Load Line Certificate, Safe Manning Document
T16_SOLAS.exp: Statutory certificates: SEC (safety equipment), SRC (safety radio), SCC (safety construction), IOPP (MARPOL), Load Line, SMC (ISM), ISSC (ISPS), MLC declaration. Validity: 5 years with intermediate surveys.

T16_SOLAS.q: What is the SOLAS requirement for number of fire drills?
T16_SOLAS.a: Fire drill at least once a month; abandon ship drill at least once a month (total combined drill every month)
opts: Fire drill at least once a month; abandon ship drill at least once a month (total combined drill every month)
T16_SOLAS.exp: SOLAS III/19: drills within 24 hours of leaving port (if >25% crew new). Thereafter: monthly. All crew participate. Log entries required. Muster stations, lifejacket donning, lifeboat stations, firefighting.

T17_MARPOL.q: How many Annexes does MARPOL have?
T17_MARPOL.exp: MARPOL 73/78 Annexes: I (Oil), II (Noxious liquid substances), III (Packaged harmful substances), IV (Sewage), V (Garbage), VI (Air pollution). Each annex addresses different type of pollution.

T17_MARPOL.q: What does MARPOL Annex I cover?
T17_MARPOL.a: Prevention of pollution by oil from ships
opts: Prevention of pollution by oil from ships
T17_MARPOL.exp: Annex I: oil pollution prevention. IOPP Certificate, Oil Record Book, 15ppm requirement for overboard discharge, Crude Oil Washing, Segregated Ballast Tanks, Double Hull requirement.

T17_MARPOL.a: Oily water overboard discharge must not exceed 15 parts per million oil content (outside special areas)
opts: Oily water overboard discharge must not exceed 15 parts per million oil content (outside special areas)
T17_MARPOL.exp: MARPOL Annex I Reg 15: bilge water may be discharged if: <15ppm oil content, ship underway, >3nm from nearest land, discharge rate monitored, OCM in use. In special areas: NIL discharge.

T17_MARPOL.q: What is the Oil Record Book?
T17_MARPOL.a: Mandatory log recording all oil operations (bilge pumping, ballast operations, tank cleaning, disposal)
opts: Mandatory log recording all oil operations (bilge pumping, ballast operations, tank cleaning, disposal)
T17_MARPOL.exp: Oil Record Book: two parts. Part I (machinery): bilge pumping, fuel transfers, sludge disposal. Part II (tankers): cargo loading, ballast, tank washing, discharge. Retained 3 years onboard.

T17_MARPOL.q: What does MARPOL Annex IV cover?
T17_MARPOL.a: Prevention of pollution by sewage from ships
opts: Prevention of pollution by sewage from ships
T17_MARPOL.exp: Annex IV: sewage must be discharged through approved sewage treatment plant (STP), comminuted/disinfected at >3nm, or held in retention tank. No discharge in port or near land.

T17_MARPOL.q: What does MARPOL Annex V cover?
T17_MARPOL.a: Prevention of pollution by garbage from ships
opts: Prevention of pollution by garbage from ships
T17_MARPOL.exp: Annex V: garbage management plan required. Garbage Record Book. Plastics: ZERO discharge anywhere. Food waste: >3nm outside special areas. Special areas (Mediterranean, Baltic): more stringent.

T17_MARPOL.q: What does MARPOL Annex VI cover?
T17_MARPOL.a: Prevention of air pollution from ships — NOx, SOx, ozone depleting substances, volatile organic compounds
opts: Prevention of air pollution from ships — NOx, SOx, ozone depleting substances, volatile organic compounds
T17_MARPOL.exp: Annex VI: NOx Tier I/II/III limits, SOx (Global 0.5% cap 2020, ECA 0.1%), ODS (no halon), VOS from tankers, Energy Efficiency (EEDI, SEEMP, CII).

T17_MARPOL.a: Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan — vessel-specific plan for improving energy efficiency
opts: Safety Equipment Examination and Maintenance Plan
Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan — vessel-specific plan for improving energy efficiency
T17_MARPOL.exp: SEEMP: MARPOL Annex VI Reg 22A. Required for all ships >5000GT. Annual review, operational measures (speed optimisation, trim, weather routing, engine maintenance). CII rating based on SEEMP implementation.

T17_MARPOL.q: What is the CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator)?
T17_MARPOL.a: Annual measure of ship's operational CO2 efficiency — rated A (best) to E (worst)
opts: Annual measure of ship's operational CO2 efficiency — rated A (best) to E (worst)
T17_MARPOL.exp: CII: IMO MARPOL Annex VI Reg 28 (2023). Annual rating. Ships rated E for 3 consecutive years must develop corrective action plan. Target: 40% reduction in carbon intensity by 2030 vs 2008 baseline.

T17_MARPOL.q: What is the purpose of the incinerator onboard?
T17_MARPOL.a: Burns solid waste, oily rags, sludge to reduce waste volume; must comply with MARPOL Annex VI standards
opts: Burns solid waste, oily rags, sludge to reduce waste volume; must comply with MARPOL Annex VI standards
T17_MARPOL.exp: Shipboard incinerator: regulated by MARPOL Annex VI Reg 16. Prohibited: plastics containing halogens, sewage sludge contaminated with cargo, PCBs. Temperature: 850–1200°C required. Not in port.

T17_MARPOL.q: What is a Special Area under MARPOL?
T17_MARPOL.a: Sea area where stricter discharge restrictions apply due to oceanographic, ecological or traffic reasons
opts: Sea area where stricter discharge restrictions apply due to oceanographic, ecological or traffic reasons
T17_MARPOL.exp: MARPOL Special Areas: Baltic Sea, Black Sea, Mediterranean, Red Sea, Gulfs, North Sea, Antarctic, Northwest European Waters. Designated per annex. In special areas: zero discharge of oil, garbage, etc.

T17_MARPOL.a: International Oil Pollution Prevention Certificate — mandatory for ships >400 GT
opts: International Oil Pollution Prevention Certificate — mandatory for ships >400 GT
T17_MARPOL.exp: IOPP Certificate: MARPOL Annex I. Valid 5 years with annual endorsements. Covers: OWS with OCM, ORB, Oil fuel system, bilge system. Surveyed by flag state or recognized organization (class society).

T18_ElecSurvey.a: Survey by class surveyor every 12 months to verify ship's class conditions are maintained
opts: Survey by class surveyor every 12 months to verify ship's class conditions are maintained
T18_ElecSurvey.exp: Annual survey: class maintains valid certificate. Surveyor checks: hull external, safety equipment, machinery, electrical systems, fire detection. Issues survey report and endorses certificate.

T18_ElecSurvey.a: Survey conducted between 2nd and 3rd annual surveys — more thorough than annual
opts: Survey conducted between 2nd and 3rd annual surveys — more thorough than annual
T18_ElecSurvey.exp: Intermediate survey: approx 2.5 years into 5-year cycle. More detailed than annual. Includes: close-up surveys of hull, testing of safety systems, machinery inspections.

T18_ElecSurvey.q: What is a special survey (renewal survey)?
T18_ElecSurvey.a: Comprehensive 5-yearly survey for renewal of class certificate — most thorough survey
opts: Comprehensive 5-yearly survey for renewal of class certificate — most thorough survey
T18_ElecSurvey.exp: Special survey: every 5 years. Drydock (hull inspection, propeller, rudder). Extensive machinery opening, testing, thickness measurements, cathodic protection check. Certificate renewed for another 5 years.

T18_ElecSurvey.a: Inspection of foreign ships by coastal state to verify compliance with international conventions
