opts: Inspection of foreign ships by coastal state to verify compliance with international conventions
T18_ElecSurvey.exp: PSC: MOU (Paris, Tokyo, etc.). Inspectors check certificates validity, safety equipment, crew familiarization, working conditions (MLC). Deficiencies → rectification. Serious deficiencies → detention.

T18_ElecSurvey.q: What electrical items are checked during class survey?
T18_ElecSurvey.a: Generator IR tests, protection relay tests, cable condition, switchboard, emergency source, fire detection
opts: Generator IR tests, protection relay tests, cable condition, switchboard, emergency source, fire detection
T18_ElecSurvey.exp: Class electrical survey: IR tests (winding insulation), relay calibration records, earth leakage system function, emergency generator auto-start test, fire detection system test, navigational lights test.

T18_ElecSurvey.q: What is a 'deficiency' in PSC inspection?
T18_ElecSurvey.a: Non-conformance with convention requirements — must be rectified by specified date
opts: Non-conformance with convention requirements — must be rectified by specified date
T18_ElecSurvey.exp: Deficiency: surveyor finds equipment not meeting convention (SOLAS, MARPOL, MLC, etc.). Rectify before departure or by specified date. Repeated deficiencies lead to targeting for future inspections.

T18_ElecSurvey.q: What is a 'detention' by port state control?
T18_ElecSurvey.a: Ship prevented from sailing due to serious deficiencies posing danger to ship, crew, or environment
opts: Ship prevented from sailing due to serious deficiencies posing danger to ship, crew, or environment
T18_ElecSurvey.exp: Detention: serious deficiencies — non-functional fire suppression, critical safety equipment failure, overdue certificates. Ship cannot sail until deficiencies rectified and verified by PSC officer.

T18_ElecSurvey.q: What is a Flag State survey?
T18_ElecSurvey.a: Survey conducted by flag state administration or recognized organization on their behalf to issue statutory certificates
opts: Survey conducted by flag state administration or recognized organization on their behalf to issue statutory certificates
T18_ElecSurvey.exp: Flag state: issues SOLAS certificates (SEC, SRC, SCC), Load Line, IOPP certificates. Mostly delegated to classification societies acting as Recognized Organizations (ROs).

T19_Tanker.q: What is an inert gas (IG) system?
T19_Tanker.a: System that maintains cargo tank atmosphere below 8% oxygen by volume to prevent explosive mixture
opts: System that maintains cargo tank atmosphere below 8% oxygen by volume to prevent explosive mixture
T19_Tanker.exp: IG: prevents explosive mixture in cargo tanks. Flammable range of oil vapour: 1–8% vapour in air. By reducing O2 to <8%, mixture outside flammable range even with vapour present. SOLAS mandatory on tankers.

T19_Tanker.a: Using cargo crude oil as washing medium to clean tanks during discharge — reduces sludge residue
opts: Using cargo crude oil as washing medium to clean tanks during discharge — reduces sludge residue
T19_Tanker.exp: COW: machines in tank spray crude oil while discharging — dissolves wax/deposits. MARPOL Annex I: mandatory for crude tankers. Reduces slop/residue. COW must be conducted under inert atmosphere.

T19_Tanker.a: Automatic valve on cargo tanks maintaining slight positive or negative pressure — prevents vapour release and structural damage
opts: Automatic valve on cargo tanks maintaining slight positive or negative pressure — prevents vapour release and structural damage
T19_Tanker.exp: P/V valve: opens slightly positive pressure during loading (vapour venting) or slight vacuum during discharge (prevents tank collapse). Set at ±2000Pa typically. Higher overpressure: P/V breaker.

T19_Tanker.q: What is a cargo stripping pump?
T19_Tanker.a: Small pump for removing last traces of cargo after main pump suction is uncovered
opts: Small pump for removing last traces of cargo after main pump suction is uncovered
T19_Tanker.exp: Stripping pump: handles low volumes and entrained vapour/air mixture that main pumps cannot handle. Eductors also used. Goal: reduce cargo residue to minimum for MARPOL compliance.

T19_Tanker.q: What gas must be checked before entering cargo tanks?
T19_Tanker.a: O2 (minimum 21%), toxic gas (H2S, benzene etc.), flammable vapour (LEL <1%)
opts: O2 (minimum 21%), toxic gas (H2S, benzene etc.), flammable vapour (LEL <1%)
T19_Tanker.exp: Tank entry: gas free certificate required. Check: O2 >21% (hypoxia risk below), hydrocarbon <1% LEL (explosion), H2S <1ppm (highly toxic). Use calibrated multi-gas detector. Continuous monitoring during entry.

T19_Tanker.a: Lower Explosive Limit — minimum concentration of flammable vapour in air that can explode with ignition source
opts: Lower Explosive Limit — minimum concentration of flammable vapour in air that can explode with ignition source
T19_Tanker.exp: LEL: below LEL, mixture too lean to ignite. Above UEL (Upper Explosive Limit), too rich. Explosive range: LEL to UEL. For gasoline: LEL ~1.4%, UEL ~7.6%. Gas detectors read % LEL.

T19_Tanker.q: What is the purpose of tank high level alarm?
T19_Tanker.a: Prevents overfilling of cargo/ballast tanks, triggering alarm before overflow occurs
opts: Prevents overfilling of cargo/ballast tanks, triggering alarm before overflow occurs
T19_Tanker.exp: High level alarm: typically set at 95–98% capacity. Operator must stop loading or transfer. Overfill protection device (OPD): if alarm ignored, automatic valve closure may be activated (tanker code).

T19_Tanker.q: What safety equipment is required before tank entry on a tanker?
T19_Tanker.a: SCBA or airline breathing apparatus, lifeline, attendant outside, communication, gas detector, emergency plan
opts: SCBA or airline breathing apparatus, lifeline, attendant outside, communication, gas detector, emergency plan
T19_Tanker.exp: Tank entry: enclosed space entry procedure (SOLAS). Permit to work. Continuous O2/gas monitoring. SCBA outside ready. Communication maintained. Emergency rescue team on standby. No smoking/naked flames.

T20_Construction.q: What is the double bottom on a ship?
T20_Construction.a: Watertight space between inner and outer hull bottom — holds ballast, fuel, or fresh water
opts: Watertight space between inner and outer hull bottom — holds ballast, fuel, or fresh water
T20_Construction.exp: Double bottom: SOLAS/Class requirement for most ships. Provides: watertight integrity (flooding of one cell doesn't flood ER), ballast capacity, fuel/water storage, structural strength.

T20_Construction.a: Empty void space between two compartments — prevents contamination between adjacent spaces (e.g. fuel and water)
opts: Empty void space between two compartments — prevents contamination between adjacent spaces (e.g. fuel and water)
T20_Construction.exp: Cofferdam: used between fuel and drinking water tanks, cargo and accommodation, fuel and cargo. Provides buffer zone — leak in one space detected before contaminating other.

T20_Construction.q: What is a Class A-60 bulkhead?
T20_Construction.a: Fire-resisting bulkhead that maintains structural integrity for 60 minutes in standard fire test — with insulation preventing heat transfer
opts: Fire-resisting bulkhead that maintains structural integrity for 60 minutes in standard fire test — with insulation preventing heat transfer
T20_Construction.exp: Class A bulkheads: steel or equivalent, standard fire test, no flame passage for 60 minutes. Suffixes: -60 (60 min insulation), -30, -15, -0. B-class: 30 min integrity, less strict construction.

T20_Construction.q: What is the purpose of watertight doors?
T20_Construction.a: Maintain watertight integrity of bulkheads in flooding scenarios — SOLAS requires remote operation and local hand operation
opts: Maintain watertight integrity of bulkheads in flooding scenarios — SOLAS requires remote operation and local hand operation
T20_Construction.exp: Watertight doors: SOLAS II-1/13. Hydraulic, electrical or hand operated. Bridge indication and control. Must close from both sides locally. Tested annually. Drills: close all doors at sea in ≤60 seconds.

T20_Construction.a: Mark on ship's hull indicating maximum permissible immersion in different seasons and ocean zones
opts: Mark on ship's hull indicating maximum permissible immersion in different seasons and ocean zones
T20_Construction.exp: Plimsoll mark/load line: LL Convention 1966. Zones: Tropical (T), Fresh (F), Tropical Fresh (TF), Summer (S), Winter (W), Winter North Atlantic (WNA). Based on reserve buoyancy and structural strength.

T21_LSA.q: What does LSA Code stand for?
T21_LSA.exp: LSA Code: adopted by IMO, mandatory under SOLAS III. Specifies detailed technical requirements for: lifejackets, immersion suits, lifebuoys, lifeboats, rescue boats, liferafts, EPIRBs, SARTs, pyrotechnics.

T21_LSA.q: What is an HRU (Hydrostatic Release Unit)?
T21_LSA.a: Automatically releases liferaft or EPIRB at water depth of 1.5–4m, allowing it to float free if ship sinks
opts: Automatically releases liferaft or EPIRB at water depth of 1.5–4m, allowing it to float free if ship sinks
T21_LSA.exp: HRU: weak link breaks at 1.5–4m water pressure, releasing securing strap. Liferaft or EPIRB floats free, painter inflates raft. Must be replaced or serviced at specified intervals (typically 2 years).

T21_LSA.a: Lifeboat launched by sliding off stern ramp — no falls/hooks required, faster and safer in heavy weather
opts: Lifeboat launched by sliding off stern ramp — no falls/hooks required, faster and safer in heavy weather
T21_LSA.exp: Free-fall lifeboat: SOLAS III/31. Slides down ramp at stern, enters water at angle. Occupants secured in seats with seatbelts. Faster than davit launch. Required on many cargo ships.

T21_LSA.a: Mechanical device (crane-like) used to lower lifeboats over ship's side
opts: Mechanical device (crane-like) used to lower lifeboats over ship's side
T21_LSA.exp: Davit types: gravity (most common — swings out, lowers by gravity), radial, articulated. SOLAS: must operate in ship with trim up to 10° and list up to 20°. Must lower boat in ≤5 minutes.

T21_LSA.q: What is a painter line on a liferaft?
T21_LSA.a: Line that attaches liferaft container to ship — pulls out CO2 inflator mechanism as ship sinks
opts: Line that attaches liferaft container to ship — pulls out CO2 inflator mechanism as ship sinks
T21_LSA.exp: Painter: 15–40m line. Ship sinks → painter reaches full extent → breaking strain exceeded or HRU releases → painter pulls inflator cord → liferaft inflates in <1 minute.

T21_LSA.q: What is a thermal protective aid (TPA)?
T21_LSA.a: Bag of waterproof insulating material providing thermal protection when immersion suit not available
opts: Bag of waterproof insulating material providing thermal protection when immersion suit not available
T21_LSA.exp: TPA: LSA Code 2.5. One TPA per lifeboat berth. Reduces heat loss for survivors who cannot don immersion suits. Quick to don. Not a substitute for immersion suit — provides limited protection.

T21_LSA.q: What are the minimum contents of a lifeboat?
T21_LSA.a: Food, water (1.5L/person/day for 3 days), first aid kit, flares, compass, bailer, sea anchor, fire extinguisher, tools, SART reflector
opts: Food, water (1.5L/person/day for 3 days), first aid kit, flares, compass, bailer, sea anchor, fire extinguisher, tools, SART reflector
T21_LSA.exp: LSA Code Chapter IV: prescribed equipment list for fully enclosed, partially enclosed motor lifeboats. Regular inspection against inventory list. Sealed rations checked for expiry. Check engine oil, fuel, battery.

T21_LSA.q: What colour must lifejackets and immersion suits be?
T21_LSA.a: Vivid redness-orange (bright orange/red) with retroreflective tape
opts: Vivid redness-orange (bright orange/red) with retroreflective tape
T21_LSA.exp: LSA Code: orange/red colour for high visibility. Retroreflective tape: reflects search lights. Light (self-igniting): SOLAS requires automatic light on lifejacket. Whistle also required.

T21_LSA.q: How often must liferafts be serviced?
T21_LSA.a: Annually at an approved service station
opts: Annually at an approved service station
T21_LSA.exp: Inflatable liferaft: annual service includes: check container, inflation gas, equipment contents, buoyancy tubes, canopy, painter, HRU. Service station certificate must be onboard. Most liferafts: 1-year service interval.

T21_LSA.a: Fast, manoeuvrable boat for recovering persons from water — separate from lifeboats
opts: Fast, manoeuvrable boat for recovering persons from water — separate from lifeboats
T21_LSA.exp: Rescue boat: SOLAS III/21. Minimum 5 persons capacity. Maximum launch time: 5 minutes. Used for MOB recovery, assisting lifeboat survivors, towing liferaft. Usually rigid inflatable (RIB) design.

T21_LSA.q: What are the requirements for lifeboat engine?
T21_LSA.a: Compression ignition, capable of running for 24 hours on full fuel, starts in ≤2 minutes from cold in 0°C
opts: Compression ignition, capable of running for 24 hours on full fuel, starts in ≤2 minutes from cold in 0°C
T21_LSA.exp: LSA Code: lifeboat engine — diesel (compression ignition), self-contained (starts without external power), forward and astern operation, fuel sufficient for 24 hours at 6 knots. Reverse propulsion system.

T21_LSA.q: What is a self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) and where required on ship?
T21_LSA.a: Air supply carried on user's back for work in oxygen-deficient or toxic atmospheres
opts: Air supply carried on user's back for work in oxygen-deficient or toxic atmospheres
T21_LSA.exp: SCBA: pressurised air cylinder (30–60 min supply), demand valve, face mask. Required by SOLAS: minimum 2 sets always ready in fire station, additional sets for cargo ships. Training required.

T22_Practical.q: What is a 'permit to work' (PTW) system?
T22_Practical.a: Formal safety procedure authorising specific hazardous work after verifying all precautions are in place
opts: Formal safety procedure authorising specific hazardous work after verifying all precautions are in place
Just a signature on a form
T22_Practical.exp: PTW: types include Hot Work, Cold Work, Enclosed Space Entry, Working at Height, Electrical Isolation. Issued by senior officer. Defines: work scope, hazards, precautions, personnel, validity period, emergency procedure.

T22_Practical.a: Procedure to isolate energy sources (electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, thermal) to prevent inadvertent energisation during maintenance
opts: Procedure to isolate energy sources (electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, thermal) to prevent inadvertent energisation during maintenance
T22_Practical.exp: LOTO: switch off → lock → tag → verify dead. Each worker attaches own lock. Equipment cannot be re-energised until all locks removed. Prevents accidental startup during maintenance — serious injury/death prevention.

T22_Practical.a: Brief pre-job safety discussion covering task hazards, controls, emergency procedures — before starting work
opts: Brief pre-job safety discussion covering task hazards, controls, emergency procedures — before starting work
T22_Practical.exp: Toolbox talk: 5–15 minutes before job starts. Review: task steps, hazards (energy, space, height, chemical), PPE required, emergency contact, stop-work authority. Signed attendance record.

T22_Practical.q: What megger voltage for a 440V motor winding?
T22_Practical.exp: IEC 60034: 500V megger for 440V and below equipment. Minimum IR before starting: 1MΩ. Drying procedure if below this. Keep megger leads away from other circuits during test.

T22_Practical.q: What is a planned maintenance system (PMS)?
T22_Practical.a: Computer-based system tracking maintenance intervals, generating job cards, recording completion
opts: Computer-based system tracking maintenance intervals, generating job cards, recording completion
T22_Practical.exp: PMS: tracks running hours, calendar intervals, records work done, parts used. Class societies increasingly require PMS records during surveys. Overdue jobs tracked and reported.

T22_Practical.a: Systematic evaluation of hazards, likelihood, severity and controls for a task before proceeding
opts: Systematic evaluation of hazards, likelihood, severity and controls for a task before proceeding
T22_Practical.exp: Risk assessment: identify hazards → assess risk (probability × severity) → implement controls → residual risk acceptable? ISM Code requires risk assessment for non-routine tasks. Document and sign off.

T22_Practical.a: Poorly ventilated space not designed for continuous occupancy — cargo holds, tanks, voids, pump rooms, cofferdams
opts: Poorly ventilated space not designed for continuous occupancy — cargo holds, tanks, voids, pump rooms, cofferdams
T22_Practical.exp: Enclosed space: O2 deficiency (inert cargo consumption), toxic gas (H2S, CO, paint fumes), flammable vapour. SOLAS III/19 & IMO MSC-CIRC.1585: pre-entry atmosphere test, ventilation, PTW mandatory.

T22_Practical.q: What is the STCW Manila Amendment related to ETO?
T22_Practical.a: Established formal ETO (Electro-Technical Officer) certification requirement as a standalone competency
opts: Established formal ETO (Electro-Technical Officer) certification requirement as a standalone competency
T22_Practical.exp: Manila 2010 Amendment: formalised ETO certification (regulation III/6). Requires: approved education and training, sea service, BST certificate, ETO certificate. Effective 2012.

T22_Practical.q: What is meant by 'dead man alarm' / UMS?
T22_Practical.a: Alarm system requiring periodic manual acknowledgement from engineer on watch — bridge alarmed if no response
opts: Alarm system requiring periodic manual acknowledgement from engineer on watch — bridge alarmed if no response
T22_Practical.exp: UMS (Unattended Machinery Space) period: engineer acknowledges alarm every 30 minutes (interval varies). No acknowledgement → escalated alarm → bridge → general alarm. Allows periodic rounds instead of continuous watch.

T22_Practical.q: What records must be maintained for electrical equipment?
T22_Practical.a: IR test records, maintenance history, relay test records, fault reports, calibration certificates — in logbook and PMS
opts: IR test records, maintenance history, relay test records, fault reports, calibration certificates — in logbook and PMS
T22_Practical.exp: Records: class surveyors check. Port state control inspectors check. ISM audit checks. Record: who did the work, when, what was found, what was done, any deviations from standard. Retained minimum 3 years.

T22_Practical.q: How do you safely test a fire detection system?
T22_Practical.a: Use approved test aerosol/heat gun on detector, verify alarm panel response, check zone, reset after test
opts: Use approved test aerosol/heat gun on detector, verify alarm panel response, check zone, reset after test
Remove detector and test at workbench
T22_Practical.exp: Monthly test: test each detector in rotation (not all same month). Test with manufacturer's test equipment. Record zone tested, detector number, person, date, result in logbook.

T22_Practical.q: What is ISM Code and what does it require?
T22_Practical.a: International Safety Management Code — requires documented SMS, Master's authority, non-conformity reporting, internal audits
opts: International Safety Management Code — requires documented SMS, Master's authority, non-conformity reporting, internal audits
T22_Practical.exp: ISM Code (SOLAS IX): company has DOC (Document of Compliance), ship has SMC (Safety Management Certificate). Elements: safety policy, responsibilities, procedures, emergency preparedness, non-conformities, internal audits.

T22_Practical.q: What are the IMO four pillars of safety?
T22_Practical.a: Life at Sea, Navigation, Prevention of Pollution, and Maritime Security
opts: Life at Sea, Navigation, Prevention of Pollution, and Maritime Security
T22_Practical.exp: IMO mission: safe, secure, efficient shipping on clean oceans. Core conventions: SOLAS (safety), MARPOL (pollution), STCW (training), ISPS (security). These represent the four main pillars.

T22_Practical.a: International Convention on Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping for Seafarers
opts: International Convention on Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping for Seafarers
T22_Practical.exp: STCW 1978 (amended 1995, Manila 2010): sets minimum training and certification standards for seafarers. Basic Safety Training (BST), watch officer certificates, specialised training (tanker, RO-RO, GMDSS).

T22_Practical.a: Reporting events that did not cause injury/damage but could have — enables learning and prevention
opts: Reporting events that did not cause injury/damage but could have — enables learning and prevention
T22_Practical.exp: Near miss: ISM Code requires near miss and non-conformity reporting. Culture: no blame — learn and improve. Reported to ISM system, investigated, corrective action documented. Used in safety briefings.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What are the two main battery types on ships?
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: Lead-acid: 2V/cell, high current output, widely used (starting, UPS). NiCad: 1.2V/cell, longer cycle life, better in extremes of temperature, used for safety systems, GMDSS batteries.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What is the electrolyte in a lead-acid battery?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Dilute sulphuric acid (H2SO4) — specific gravity 1.20–1.28 when charged
opts: Dilute sulphuric acid (H2SO4) — specific gravity 1.20–1.28 when charged
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: Lead-acid: H2SO4 reacts with PbO2 (+) and Pb (-) plates during discharge. During charge, H2SO4 concentration increases (SG rises). SG check with hydrometer: 1.20 = discharged, 1.28 = fully charged.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What is the electrolyte in a NiCad battery?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) solution — specific gravity does NOT change with charge state
opts: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) solution — specific gravity does NOT change with charge state
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: NiCad/alkaline: KOH electrolyte. Unlike lead-acid, SG doesn't change with charge state — cannot test charge by SG. Check state of charge by voltage measurement or capacity test.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What gas is produced during battery charging?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Hydrogen gas — highly flammable, explosive at 4–75% concentration in air
opts: Hydrogen gas — highly flammable, explosive at 4–75% concentration in air
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: Both lead-acid and NiCad produce hydrogen during overcharge/gassing phase. Hydrogen: LEL 4%, UEL 75%, autoignition 565°C. Battery rooms: explosion-proof fittings, no open flames, ventilate before and during charging.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What is the purpose of battery room ventilation?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Remove hydrogen gas produced during charging to below explosive limits (minimum 12 air changes per hour)
opts: Remove hydrogen gas produced during charging to below explosive limits (minimum 12 air changes per hour)
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: SOLAS: battery rooms require forced ventilation. Exhaust from top (hydrogen is lighter than air). Inlet near floor. Fan: explosion-proof type. Ventilation must operate continuously during charging.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What is 'specific gravity' and how is it measured?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Density of electrolyte relative to water — measured with hydrometer; indicates charge state in lead-acid batteries
opts: Density of electrolyte relative to water — measured with hydrometer; indicates charge state in lead-acid batteries
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: Hydrometer: floating glass ball in tube. Draw electrolyte sample, read float level. SG 1.28 = fully charged. SG 1.20 = discharged. Also shows electrolyte condition — should be clear, not brown.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What is the rated capacity of a battery?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Ampere-hours (Ah) — product of discharge current and time: e.g. 100Ah = 5A for 20 hours
opts: Ampere-hours (Ah) — product of discharge current and time: e.g. 100Ah = 5A for 20 hours
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: Capacity depends on discharge rate: C10 (10-hour rate) or C20. Discharging faster reduces capacity. Temperature also affects: cold reduces capacity. State of charge = remaining Ah.

T23_BatteriesDC.a: Small constant current maintaining battery at full charge without gassing — used for standby batteries
opts: Small constant current maintaining battery at full charge without gassing — used for standby batteries
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: Trickle charge: compensates self-discharge. Rate: 1–5% of Ah capacity. Keeps emergency batteries always ready. Boost/equalisation charge periodically needed to desulfate lead-acid plates.

T23_BatteriesDC.a: Overcharge at low rate for extended period — equalises voltage of all cells and removes sulphation
opts: Overcharge at low rate for extended period — equalises voltage of all cells and removes sulphation
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: Equalisation: done monthly or quarterly. Voltage per cell rises to ~2.5–2.7V (lead-acid), gassing occurs. Ensures all cells fully charged and sulphation removed. Requires good ventilation.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What are the safety precautions when working on batteries?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: PPE (goggles, gloves), no open flames, ventilate, no metallic tools near terminals, isolate before work, acid kit available
opts: PPE (goggles, gloves), no open flames, ventilate, no metallic tools near terminals, isolate before work, acid kit available
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: Battery hazards: H2SO4 (acid burns), H2 gas (explosion), high short circuit current (burns from tools). First aid: flush acid with water immediately. Fire extinguisher: CO2 or dry powder.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What is a UPS battery and how is it maintained?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Sealed lead-acid (VRLA) typically — maintenance: check voltage, capacity test, replace at end-of-life (~3–5 years)
opts: Sealed lead-acid (VRLA) typically — maintenance: check voltage, capacity test, replace at end-of-life (~3–5 years)
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: VRLA (Valve Regulated Lead Acid) / AGM / Gel: sealed, no topping up, recombines gas internally. Maintenance: measure terminal voltage, conduct annual/biennial capacity test (discharge to verify Ah capacity), replace at EOL.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What is the 24V DC system used for on ships?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Emergency lighting, GMDSS equipment, navigation instruments, alarms — battery backed essential services
opts: Emergency lighting, GMDSS equipment, navigation instruments, alarms — battery backed essential services
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: 24V DC: from battery backed charger-rectifier system. Provides power to: navigation lights (emergency), GMDSS radio, fire alarm, crew alarm, UMS monitoring, PA system — continues through blackout.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What is the 110V DC system used for on some ships?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Main source for older electric propulsion, emergency switchboard supply, some deck machinery control
opts: Main source for older electric propulsion, emergency switchboard supply, some deck machinery control
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: 110V DC: historically common for deck machinery control (Ward Leonard drives), some older ships use for emergency distribution. Modern ships increasingly 24V or 48V DC systems.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: How do you perform a capacity test on a battery?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Fully charge, then discharge at rated current (C10 or C20 rate), measure time to reach minimum voltage
opts: Fully charge, then discharge at rated current (C10 or C20 rate), measure time to reach minimum voltage
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: Capacity test: confirms battery can deliver rated Ah. Required by class for SOLAS essential battery systems (emergency lighting, GMDSS). Perform annually or biannually. Replace if capacity <80% of rated.

T23_BatteriesDC.q: What are signs of battery deterioration?
T23_BatteriesDC.a: Reduced capacity, increased self-discharge, bulging case, leaking electrolyte, excessive gassing, plate sulphation, discolouration
opts: Reduced capacity, increased self-discharge, bulging case, leaking electrolyte, excessive gassing, plate sulphation, discolouration
T23_BatteriesDC.exp: End-of-life signs: capacity below 80%, cell voltage inconsistency, white sulphate deposit on lead-acid plates, cracked case, electrolyte browning. Plan replacement — don't wait for failure in emergency.
